extracted.intended_audience: physicians and clinical laboratory technicians performing gastric-juice (suc gastrique) analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural laboratory protocols and interpretive criteria for collecting, testing, and interpreting human gastric juice (suc gastrique) including acid determinations, detection of specific organic acids, assays of digestive ferments, and assessment of digestion products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected gastric juice volume and sampling timing
rubrics_metrics.description: «en  principe … on n’en retire guère plus, ordinairement, de 40 à 50 centimètres cubes»; extraction usually 1½ to 2 hours after test meal (Germain Sée) or earlier (½ hour) if yield is insignificant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If quantity deviates notably the physician must draw conclusions; if yield is very small or nil, repeat the test meal and perform extraction much earlier (e.g. ½ hour). Use Germain Sée meat test meal when indicated (recipe provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Macroscopic appearance and odor as diagnostic clues
rubrics_metrics.description: La matière retirée «se présente ordinairement sous forme d’une bouillie blanchâtre, plus ou moins fluide»; odor generally faint if digestion normal, vinegar/ rancid butter smells indicate pathology; can be fetid in gastric carcinoma.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record colour, consistency and odor; vinegar or rancid butter odors suggest organic pathology (e.g., fermentation, butyric/acetic acids) and may guide which chemical tests to perform first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration procedure and mucus indication
rubrics_metrics.description: «on commence par filtrer la moitié environ du liquide gastrique obtenu. La lenteur … de la filtration sera l’indice de la présence du mucus».
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter about half the sample; examine filtration residue visually/microscopically for mucus and other indications of digestion; retain unfiltered portion for additional tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial acidity check before further tests
rubrics_metrics.description: «On s’assurera d’abord, à l’aide d’un papier de tournesol plongé dedans, que ce liquide est bien acide.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always confirm the sample is acidic (rarely neutral/alkaline) before proceeding; acidity status determines which ferment tests are meaningful (pepsin requires acid).

rubrics_metrics.name: Günzburg (phloroglucinovanillic) reaction for organic HCl
rubrics_metrics.description: Réactif de Günzburg (phloroglucine 2g, vanilline 1g, alcool absolu 10gr). Mix a few drops with equal quantity of gastric juice, heat gently; presence of combined (organic) HCl gives a red-purple coloration, especially at edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare reagent fresh and protect from light; heat in bain-marie (not direct flame). Organic acids do not react. Beware false positives (e.g., acidic calcium phosphate). Use a confirmatory test (Boas) if uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boas reagent as confirmatory test for HCl
rubrics_metrics.description: Réactif de Boas (résorcine 0.50g, sucre de canne 0.30g, alcool 60° 10 cc) used like Günzburg; red rim indicates HCl presence but reaction is less sensitive and slower.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Boas reaction to control/confirm Günzburg results when needed; do not rely solely on the less sensitive Boas reaction for faint positives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ulfermann reaction for lactic acid (use on ether extract)
rubrics_metrics.description: Réactif d’Ulfermann: solution d’acide picrique 4% 10 cc, eau distillée 20 cc, perchlorure de fer 1 drop. Addition of lactic acid/lactate turns blue-violet to yellow-serin; HCl decolorizes the mix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid interferences, operate on the ether extract of the gastric juice (shake with ether several times, collect and evaporate). Avoid excess reagent; prepare reagent fresh and use on residue dissolved in water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ether extraction for organic acids (lactic, acetic, butyric)
rubrics_metrics.description: «quelques centimètres cubes… sont agités… avec leur volume d’éther… Les solutés éthérés sont décantés, rassemblés… et évaporés.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform multiple ether extractions (3–4 times) of a measured volume, combine ether phases, evaporate to residue, redissolve residue in water and apply specific reagents. Distillation is an alternative, especially for volatile acids like butyric acid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of acetic acid (perchloride of iron and ethyl acetate test)
rubrics_metrics.description: After ether extraction and evaporation, neutralize with dilute NaOH; add perchloride of iron to yield red-brown colour (iron acetate). Alternatively evaporate half to dryness, take up in alcohol, add concentrated sulfuric acid and warm — characteristic acetic ether smell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neutralize cautiously; concentrate if needed. Use both reactions for confirmation. Prepare reagents freshly. Smell test requires caution for safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection of butyric acid (ether separation or distillation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat 10–13 cc with equal volume of ether several times, evaporate, dissolve residue in warm water, add small fragments of CaCl2 — oily droplets with rancid butter odour indicate butyric acid. Distillation (butyric b.p. 163°C) generally gives better results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distillation in small glass retort heated in sand bath recommended for better isolation. Use CaCl2 to cause separation if performing ether extraction. Odor is a strong diagnostic cue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total acidity titration (acidimetry) with phenolphthalein
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce 10 cc non-filtered gastric juice, add 3–4 drops alcoholic phenolphthalein, titrate with decinormal NaOH until a persistent pink appears. Each cc of NaOH corresponds to 0.0365 g HCl; multiply to express acidity of 10 cc in HCl equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare decinormal NaOH by dissolving NaOH (4 g) in boiled distilled water to 1000 cc (verify titration if needed). Agitate constantly during titration. Alternative: use litmus paper via the touch method if preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal and pathological acidity ranges and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: «L’acidité normale… varie… de 1,5 à 2 °/oo… D’après… Bouveret, variations comprise entre 0,8 et 6 °/oo; acidités supérieures à 4 °/oo dues à acide chlorhydrique — signe d’hyperchlorhydrie; very low acidities suggest secretion slowing, cancer, nervous dyspepsia, atrophy of gastric mucosa.»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measured acidity (in HCl equivalents per 10 cc or per mille) to classify hyperchlorhydria, hypochlorhydria, or achlorhydria and guide further tests and clinical interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of HCl combined in organic compounds (Sjöqvist principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Add excess barium carbonate to 5–10 cc non-filtered gastric juice, evaporate to dryness, incinerate to ashes; soluble chloride (barium chloride) remains and is exhausted with hot water (~40–50 cc) and the barium is assayed as sulfate (classical method) to deduce HCl combined amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incinerate progressively (alcohol lamp then red heat) to complete combustion; extract ashes repeatedly to collect about 40–50 cc filtrate for barium assay. Subtract bound-HCl equivalent from total acidity to obtain acidity due to organic acids and mineral acids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total chloride determination by soda carbonated ignition and argentimetric titration
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain total chlorine: to 5 cc add excess pure sodium carbonate (1 g), evaporate to dryness and calcine; chlorine remains in ashes as sodium chloride; dissolve ashes and titrate chloride as silver chloride (argentimetry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when total chlorine content is required; ensure complete combustion and proper dissolution of ash before AgCl titration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: check ferments (pepsin and labferment) and acidity interdependence
rubrics_metrics.description: Pepsin acts only in acidic medium of adequate degree; labferment acts in acid or neutral but not alkaline. Therefore acidity determination is prerequisite to ferment assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always determine acidity before pepsin/labferment testing because low/absent acid may mask enzyme activity; adjust (add HCl) when necessary to activate pro-enzymes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pepsin qualitative/activity assay by artificial digestion of standardized egg-white cubes
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare equal-weight cooked egg-white cubes (e.g., 5 centigrammes), suspend one cube in 10–20 cc filtered gastric juice, incubate at 39°C; monitor until cube dissolves. Shorter dissolution time indicates more pepsin — but acid quantity also influences rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reduce acid-dependence error, perform three simultaneous digestions: (1) gastric juice alone, (2) gastric juice + equal volume HCl 2 ‰, (3) gastric juice + added pepsin — compare digestion times to distinguish pepsin vs acid deficiency. If sample lacks HCl, add HCl 4 ‰ dropwise until Günzburg positive before testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concluding absence of pepsin/propepsin on complete digestion failure
rubrics_metrics.description: If, after proper acidification and control additions, digestion completely fails, conclude the sample lacks both pepsin and propepsin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adequate acidification (Günzburg reaction positive) before concluding absence; include controls with added pepsin and HCl to rule out procedural errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labferment (rennin) qualitative test by milk coagulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduce filtered gastric juice (10 cc), neutralize exactly with dilute sodium carbonate or lime water, add equal volume of boiled milk, incubate at 38°C. Coagulation within ~15 minutes indicates presence of labferment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neutralization must be precise to destroy endogenous labferment inhibitors; use boiled milk to avoid extraneous enzymes. Observe time to coagulation as index of activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labzymogene identification and conversion to labferment
rubrics_metrics.description: To test labzymogene: alkalinize gastric juice to destroy labferment, add 2–3 cc of 1/100 chlorure de calcium, add equal volume milk, incubate at 38°C; coagulation after 10–15 minutes indicates presence of labzymogene. If juice lacks HCl, add HCl 4 ‰ and incubate 2–3 hours at 38°C to convert labzymogene into labferment then repeat coagulation test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alkalinization should be firm but slight; CaCl2 facilitates coagulation. Activation step (adding HCl and incubating) is necessary if initial juice is achlorhydric to reveal labzymogene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate quantification of labferment and labzymogene by serial dilution
rubrics_metrics.description: Make serial dilutions of the gastric juice (1/10, 1/20, 1/30, …). Take 10 cc of each, neutralize exactly, add 10 cc milk and incubate at 38°C. Normal labferment yields coagulation at dilutions up to 1/30–1/40; labzymogene (after activation) may coagulate at up to 1/100–1/150.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dilution endpoint (highest dilution giving coagulation) as semi-quantitative measure of ferment abundance (Boas observations cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of starch (amylaceous) digestion with iodine and Fehling tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Iodine colours: soluble starch blue, erythrodextrin red, achroodextrin no colour. A normal gastric sample from Ewald test-meal should not stain with iodine (no soluble starch/erythrodextrin). For reducing sugars, mix 1 cc sample with equal volume Fehling's solution and boil — reduction indicates maltose/advanced starch digestion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret iodine and Fehling together: red/violet with iodine and little Fehling reduction indicates incomplete salivary digestion; strong Fehling reduction and absence of iodine colour indicate advanced starch digestion to maltose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of protein (albuminoids) digestion via heat coagulation, neutralization, precipitation series, and biuret
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat filtered (acid) gastric juice: appearance of coagulum indicates undigested albumin. Filter out coagulum, neutralize — new precipitate indicates syntonine. Treat sample with ferrocyanide of potassium (acetic) or nitric acid to detect propeptone (heat will dissolve cold precipitate). Saturation with sulfate of magnesium/ammonium precipitates propeptone. Finally, biuret reaction (CuSO4 + NaOH) identifies peptone (violet- amethystine/rose coloration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the sequence (heat → filter → neutralize → ferrocyanide/nitric acid → sulfate precipitation → biuret) to distinguish albumin, syntonine, propeptone, and peptone. Intensity/abundance of precipitates and biuret colour give semi-quantitative information about digestion stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive profile of normal digestion products
rubrics_metrics.description: In normal digestion from appropriate test meals: albumin and syntonine should be absent or trace; propeptone and peptone should predominate and give a strong biuret reaction (intense violet-amethystine/rose). For amylaceous digestion, absence of iodine reactivity and positive Fehling reduction indicate normal progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use expected profile as benchmark; deviations indicate impaired digestion (e.g., excess acid inhibiting ptyalin, low pepsin/ferment activity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization of tests when sample volume is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: «… on devra d’abord procéder à la détermination de l’acidité…, puis chercher à caractériser le labferment et le labzymogène. On pratiquera ensuite la réaction du biuret…»
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When gastric juice volume is insufficient to perform all tests (often only 40–50 cc or less), perform (in order): total acidity measurement, labferment/labzymogene characterization (coagulation tests), then biuret reaction for peptones; reserve other tests as sample allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: General reagent/handling precautions
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple advisories: prepare reagents «autant que possible… au moment du besoin»; conserve some reagents «à l’abri de la lumière»; heat gently in bain-marie rather than direct flame; avoid using excess reagent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare sensitive reagents fresh and store protected from light; perform heating steps in bain-marie; avoid reagent excess which can mask reactions; be aware of interfering substances (e.g., phosphates, sugars, alcohol producing false Ulfermann reaction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Germain Sée test meal composition when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided recipe for Germain Sée meal (e.g., stale bread 100 gr, well-trimmed and minced meat 60 gr, water 200 gr) recommended when meat-containing meal is needed for albuminoid digestion assessment; extraction 1½–2 hours after meal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this standardized test meal when assessing albuminoid digestion to yield adequate substrates (meat) to evaluate pepsin/labferment activity and digestion product profile.
